newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN 2006 OLO YIELD BELOW 6.00 PCT, SEEN LOWER.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN 2006 OLO YIELD BELOW 6.00 PCT, SEEN LOWER.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds climbed strongly on Thursday, and traders said there seemed no end in sight to the rally that pushed the benchmark 10-year OLO yield down through six percent for the first time.
"The market just wants to go higher, it is looking for any excuse," one trader said.

The catalyst for Thursday afternoon's rally was neutral consumer price and retail sales figures from the United States that at first caused a slight dip then attracted a spate of professional buying, traders said. End users were nowhere in sight, they added.
"The only way to be in this market is long," one trader said. "The shorts have been squeezed out."
But traders lamented that the market remained illiquid, accentuating any move.
"There is a liquidity squeeze...the real volume is very low," one trader said.
Traders noted that while the Belgian market had tracked German Bunds in the afternoon, it had not aped the curve flattening seen there.
"Our curve remained pretty much unchanged or, if anything, moved slightly steeper," one trader said.
The benchmark 2006 OLO ended the day yielding a record low 5.98 percent from Wednesday's 6.01 percent, although the spread over Bunds ticked out to 16 basis points from 15.
The December futures contract was 19 basis points higher at 120.24.
